newsitem.title: UK: China shipment talk sends UK wheat futures up.
newsitem.headline: China shipment talk sends UK wheat futures up.

text.p: Talk that 50,000 tonnes of wheat is going to be loaded in March for shipment to China has sent UK LIFFE wheat futures up, traders said.
By 1210 GMT active May wheat was up 1.25 stg at 98.45 stg.
Traders were sceptical. One exporter confirmed that there was a vessel due to load in Tilbury, but said he could not confirm that it was going to China.
"There's a lot of rumour flying around," he said. "One has to be a little bit sceptical."
"That's the rumour in the market," another said of the China shipment.
Port sources declined to confirm or deny the rumour.
The rise underlined an improving UK supply position, the trader said.
"We seem to be able to offer wheat when a lot of people can't," he said. "The market is fundamentally strong on third country (non-EU) demand."
At current price levels the UK could export. "The surplus we had doesn't look so much of a problem," he said. But he was concerned that sharp price rises could undermine competitiveness.
The rise came despite a firm pound this morning, traders said. Better than expected UK trade data helped sterling against other European currencies.
Sterling strength usually has a direct negative effect on UK grains futures. But today the market was ignoring sterling, traders said.
